q: In Fig. 4 (age-distribution prevalence per 100000 males on December 31, 2007), which age band shows the highest combined HA+HB prevalence?
fact: In the line chart at the top of the page, the diamond-marked HA+HB trace peaks at the 26-30 tick (about 0.97), above its neighbours at 21-25 (about 0.88) and 31-35 (about 0.75).
why_arbitrary: Where a measured prevalence curve peaks across age bands is an empirical feature of this Taiwanese registry data, not something fixed by convention.

q: In Figure 2 (parts of the interface between Omega^(1)_eps and the thin fracture R_eps), which of the three labeled interface curves is the one lying on the boundary of the node R^(0)_eps rather than on a thin rectangle?
fact: In the figure above the caption, the leader arrow from the middle label Gamma^(1,0)_eps points at the small bulge where the three thin strips meet (the node), while Gamma^(1,1)_eps points at the horizontal strip's upper edge and Gamma^(1,2)_eps at the upper-right strip.
why_arbitrary: Which of the three labels sits on the node rather than on a rectangle side is set by this paper's own index bookkeeping and by where the arrows land in this drawing.
note: The j=0 convention is also stated in the prose after (2.5), so a reader with only the text could reach the same answer; the figure's arrows confirm it independently.

q: In the leftmost panel of FIG. 14 (cumulative S/N versus instrument noise sensitivity sigma_noise), what cumulative S/N does the Hα×HeII cross-correlation curve at z = 5 reach at the solid vertical line marking the current CDIM configuration?
stem_edit: Added 'solid' before 'vertical line': the panel carries three vertical lines and the CDIM/SPHEREx/CDIM+ text labels sit in the second panel, so the caption's 'CDIM is solid' is the identifier.
fact: In the leftmost panel, the solid blue (Hα×HeII, z = 5) curve crosses the solid black vertical line at just above 2 on the logarithmic S/N axis, in the white region above the shaded S/N < 1 band.
why_arbitrary: The predicted S/N at the CDIM sensitivity comes from this paper's fiducial model and instrument specifications, so it can only be read off the plotted curve.

q: In the Power-Supply Current vs Digital Input Code plot taken with the internal reference enabled and gain = 1, what is the power-supply current at a digital input code of 32768?
fact: Figure 70 (middle-right panel, annotated 'Internal reference enabled, Gain = 1') shows the trace flat just above the 0.6 gridline at the 32768 tick, roughly 0.65 mA.
why_arbitrary: The plateau current of this particular DAC with its internal reference on is a measured device characteristic, not a value implied by the axis scale.
note: The companion external-reference plot (Figure 69) sits at about 0.25 mA, which is the first distractor's source.

q: In the Functional Block Diagram of Section 7.2, how many driver channels are shown in the TIN-to-TOUT path (the number annotated on that path)?
fact: In the block diagram under 7.2, the slash marks on both the TIN input and the TOUT RS232 output of the TX driver triangle carry the numeral 2.
why_arbitrary: The channel count is a property of this specific MAX232 part rather than a generic block-diagram convention; the same page also shows 4 (capacitors) and 5 (the 5V supply).

q: In Figure 12 (Offset Voltage vs Common-Mode Voltage), at what common-mode voltage do the five typical units show the marked step in VOS?
fact: In the bottom-right panel (Figure 12), the annotation 'VCM = -18.1 V' with its leader arrow sits at the left-hand vertical line where the five traces break, just right of the -20 V axis end.
why_arbitrary: The exact common-mode voltage at which this amplifier's input stage transitions is a measured device number, not a round axis value.

q: In Figure 45 (Maximum Output Voltage vs Frequency), what peak-to-peak output voltage does the VS = ±15 V curve deliver at 1 MHz?
fact: In the middle-left panel (Figure 45), the blue VS = ±15 V trace has rolled off from its 30 VPP plateau, merged with the ±5 V trace near 10 VPP, and sits at roughly 6 VPP where the curve crosses the 1M frequency tick.
why_arbitrary: The slew-rate-limited output amplitude at 1 MHz follows from this amplifier's measured slew rate, so only the plotted curve gives it.
note: Below about 700 kHz the ±15 V and ±5 V traces coincide (the red trace is drawn on top), so the reading is taken from the merged curve.

q: In the EXAMPLE STENCIL DESIGN / SOLDER PASTE EXAMPLE drawing for the DGK0008A VSSOP package, what is the long-side dimension of each of the eight solder-paste apertures?
fact: The callout '8X (1.4)' at the top of the drawing spans the horizontal (long) extent of an aperture, while '8X (0.45)' at the left spans its short vertical extent.
why_arbitrary: The aperture length for this package's stencil is a specific recommended value; 0.65 (pin pitch) and 4.4 (span across the two rows) are the neighbouring callouts.

q: In Figure 5-31 (D1, D2 Primary-Side Output Switch Voltage Swing vs Current at VCC = 3.3 V), what is the VD1/VD2 voltage swing at a switching current of 100 mA?
fact: In the left plot (Figure 5-31), the falling trace sits just above the 3.10 gridline where it crosses the 100 mA gridline, about one fifth of the way up to 3.20.
why_arbitrary: The switch voltage drop versus current is measured silicon behaviour, so the value only exists on this curve.
note: The 4.87 V distractor is the VCC = 5 V companion curve (Figure 5-32) at the same 100 mA.

q: In Figure 7-4 (Pulse-Width-Modulation vs Control Voltage), what output duty cycle does the 'Clock period = 2.5 RC' curve give at a control voltage of 2.5 V?
fact: In Figure 7-4, the red 'Clock period = 2.5 RC' curve passes through roughly 30% duty cycle at the 2.5 V tick, while the black 1 RC curve is near 75% there.
why_arbitrary: The nonlinear RC-charging transfer curve is specific to this timer and clock-period ratio, so the duty cycle at 2.5 V cannot be inferred from the axes.

q: In Figure 32 (Shutdown Supply Current and Output Voltage vs Time, VDD = 15 V), what is the supply current per channel before the shutdown pulse is applied?
fact: In the bottom trace of the left figure (Figure 32), the supply current sits flat a little above the 0.75 gridline for t < 0, then drops to about 0.4 and settles near 0.1 mA/Ch during shutdown.
why_arbitrary: The quiescent supply current per channel at VDD = 15 V is a measured device value, not one of the labelled gridlines.
